bullets.title: Semis momentum unwind underway but viewed as technical, not fundamental
bullets.body: The semiconductor sector dropped 11%+ over two days in early July, driven by positioning/de-grossing and Samsung's record-but-disappointingly-received Q2 results, NVDA's Kyber rack delay to 2028, and DeepSeek developing its own AI chip. Multiple banks (JPM, MS, 22V) characterized the selloff as positioning/technical—memory/semi pricing remains structurally bullish (DRAM up 20-30% Q3, NAND up 35-40%), supply deficits extend to 2028, and AI capex guidance from hyperscalers kept rising. Semi stocks with >14% YTD gains led the bounce by week's end.

bullets.title: META's AI compute expansion and model launches drive sharp re-rating
bullets.body: Meta reported plans to double compute capacity to 14GW by 2027 (~$250B capex vs prior $175-225B street), launched Muse Spark 1.1 (competitive with Anthropic/OpenAI at ~25% lower cost), and began monetizing AI via developer APIs. Multiple analysts raised price targets (KeyBanc to $790, Mizuho upgraded, Erste Group to buy). Stock gained ~19% in July through the digest window. Meta also revealed its in-house Iris AI chip entering production in September with Broadcom as design partner and TSMC as manufacturer.

bullets.title: US-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption weigh on macro; oil spikes
bullets.body: Trump declared the ceasefire with Iran 'over,' US forces struck 80+ Iranian targets, and tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz dropped sharply. Brent crude surged toward $80 before pulling back. Goldman and IEA warned the escalation could upend oil supply surplus forecasts. Iran and Oman were simultaneously in talks on Hormuz navigational mechanisms. Prediction markets pushed Hormuz normalization to December at earliest. US banks and Iran engaged in parallel diplomatic back-channels via Qatar and Oman.

bullets.title: Fed signals hawkish pivot; September hike odds rise to ~37%; 30-year yields at 5%+
bullets.body: Governor Waller's speech stated inflation risks have 'completely flipped' relative to labor market risks, and forward guidance may impair policy transmission. June FOMC minutes showed a few participants already saw a case for hiking. Market-implied September hike probability rose to ~37% per StreetAccount prediction market data. The 30-year Treasury auction cleared at 5.058%, highest since pre-GFC. JPM's desk sees 10yr fair value drifting toward 4.5%, with risk skewed higher.

bullets.title: Goldman's AI inflation note: memory/chip prices adding 0.2-0.5% to core PCE
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs published that AI-induced increases in memory, software, and electricity costs were already adding more than 0.2 percentage points to core PCE year-over-year, rising to an estimated 0.5% by year-end. This is contributing to the Fed's more hawkish tilt and has been flagged in the Fed's semi-annual Monetary Policy Report, which explicitly cited AI-related factors as an inflation driver.

bullets.title: Micron raises US capex to $250B through 2035; NY fab concrete poured
bullets.body: Micron increased its planned US manufacturing investment from $200B to $250B+ through 2035, began concrete work on its New York DRAM megafab, and signed a strategic long-term supply agreement with Ford. The company also disclosed 16 total strategic customer agreements (SCAs), seen as a floor on volumes. Q3 results showed 84.9% gross margins, ~320bps above consensus. SK Hynix's Nasdaq debut (priced at $149, opened at $170-180, 7x oversubscribed for $26.5B) underscored the AI memory supercycle narrative.

bullets.title: Apple-Broadcom $30B+ deal through 2031 for custom AI silicon and RF chips
bullets.body: Apple and Broadcom announced a multi-year agreement exceeding $30B through 2031 for custom silicon (including new ASIC for Apple Private Cloud Compute) and wireless connectivity components. The deal will produce 15B+ US-made chips and involves $1.5B of capex for Broadcom's Fort Collins facility. Analysts viewed it as extending Broadcom's role into AI datacenter XPUs for Apple, with a meaningful ramp expected around 2029-2030 as Apple's LLM matures.

bullets.title: Price momentum factor in worst drawdown since 2022; rotation to hyperscalers favored
bullets.body: The price momentum factor fell ~17-23% from its June 22 peak in one of the worst short-period drawdowns since the dotcom era. Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson recommended rotating from semis to hyperscalers. 22V Research and JPM both flagged EPS momentum as more resilient than price momentum. By week-end, momentum showed signs of stabilizing, and most banks maintained tactical bullish views citing strong earnings revisions (+3.4% vs -2% 5-yr avg) and consumer resilience.

bullets.title: UBS proprietary market fragility index and Shiller PE both hit historic highs
bullets.body: UBS's proprietary market fragility index hit an all-time high heading into earnings season. Separately, the Shiller P/E ratio approached its dot-com bubble peak. Options traders reached their most bullish positioning since December 2020, with put/call ratios at 0.61. SPY had a $5.9B positive gamma wall at 755 providing near-term support.

bullets.title: Tech was the sole S&P 500 outperforming sector in Q2—first time since 1990
bullets.body: Bespoke noted that Q2 2026 was the first quarter since at least 1990 in which only one S&P 500 sector—Technology—outperformed the index. Q2 top-performing tech stocks were already lagging in Q3, with nearly all of the top 20 H1 performers in the red through early July. The Shiller P/E forward-trailing gap was near its widest on record, typically seen at market extremes.

bullets.title: DeepSeek developing its own AI chip; Chinese firms shifting 46% of AI budgets to domestic hardware
bullets.body: Reuters reported DeepSeek is developing a proprietary AI inference chip to reduce reliance on Nvidia and Huawei. Separately, a survey found Chinese executives plan to allocate 46% of AI accelerator budgets to domestic products vs. 30% today. China's Ministry of Commerce was also discussing restricting overseas access to advanced homegrown AI models. These developments weighed on semiconductor stocks early in the week before the broader selloff was attributed to technical positioning.

bullets.title: Apple sues OpenAI alleging trade secret theft by ex-employees
bullets.body: Apple filed a federal lawsuit against OpenAI alleging misappropriation of trade secrets, including hardware files and manufacturing practices. The suit accuses OpenAI's Chief Hardware Officer Tang Tan and engineer Chang Liu of taking confidential information. OpenAI has hired approximately 400 former Apple employees. Apple also secured an exemption from semiconductor tariffs in exchange for committing to manufacture Mac and iPhone chips at Intel fabs.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex race intensifies: Google interest expense 15x YoY; Amazon raises $25B
bullets.body: Google's quarterly interest expense exceeded $500M, up 15x year-over-year, as the company finances its AI buildout. Amazon priced a $25B eight-tranche bond sale and guided $200B+ capex for 2026. JPMorgan downgraded MSFT and META credit on AI capex financing risks while upgrading Oracle to Overweight as the 'most attractive hyperscaler value.' MS raised Google's 2027-2028 capex forecasts to $350B and $375B respectively.

bullets.title: NVDA at 10-year relative P/E low vs S&P 500 despite AI compute scarcity
bullets.body: With NVDA's stock near flat YTD and at its lowest forward P/E relative to the S&P 500 in a decade (10%+ discount), multiple banks flagged it as attractively valued. NVDA's NDR with Morgan Stanley highlighted accelerating growth toward $100B quarterly revenue, with GPU rental rates up 5-10% YTD. Anthropic's compute share on NVDA chips reportedly approached 50%. The Kyber rack delay was partially offset by confirmation that Rubin Ultra roadmap remained on track.

bullets.title: US power demand hits all-time record; electricity prices seen continuing to surge
bullets.body: PJM hit an all-time peak load record of 168,158 MW. Goldman Sachs noted US electricity prices are rising sharply due to relentless data center demand. Taiwan semiconductor exports surged to $133B in H1 2026 (+44% YoY) as AI supply chain demand accelerated, with ATP imports touching $100B in May. China also hit a record electricity load driven by data center and EV demand.

bullets.title: TeraWulf secures $19B Anthropic 20-year data center lease; AI infrastructure deals proliferating
bullets.body: TeraWulf announced a 20-year lease with Anthropic at its Justified Data Campus (401MW, ~$19B contracted revenue) starting H2 2027. IREN also rallied on Anthropic's reported plans for 1.4GW of Australian data center capacity. Analysts raised WULF price targets to $36-72 range. The week also saw Apollo's $35B AI chip credit facility enter secondary markets, signaling expanding AI financing infrastructure.

bullets.title: NFLX engagement declining; exploring live TV and bundles to retain subscribers
bullets.body: Netflix engagement (watch time, completion rates) declined despite healthy subscriber retention. The company explored live TV channels, bundling with Peacock, and potential bids for 2030-2034 FIFA World Cup rights. JPMorgan cut the price target to $118 maintaining Overweight, citing 325M+ subscribers at an under-penetrated ~47% of CTV households globally. Citi cut PT to $100 from $115 on multiple compression risk.

bullets.title: AI token price competition intensifying; open-source Chinese models at 30%+ of US enterprise usage
bullets.body: Brad Gerstner flagged companies will pay 5x more for best-in-class AI with no evidence of pricing pressure from open source. However, Morgan Stanley data showed Chinese AI models (DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM) already represent >30% of US company token usage vs. 11% historically. Anthropic token costs are being compared to alternatives at 23x premiums. OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol claims 54% more token efficiency on agentic coding at 1/3 the cost of competitors.

bullets.title: Macro: S&P 0.5% from all-time high; markets close modestly higher after Iran-driven volatility
bullets.body: The S&P 500 closed at 7,573.60 (+0.40%) on Friday, July 10, roughly 0.5% from an all-time high. Nasdaq closed +0.28% at 26,280.70. The week saw significant volatility—oil spiked to near $80 on Iran strikes before fading back to ~$71-76. Credit spreads widened modestly on geopolitical risk. AAII bull-bear spread improved from -10.9% to -0.9% during the period. Q2 EPS estimates were revised up 3.4% vs a typical -2% decline, the strongest revision since Q2 2021.
